title: Attention fusion prober and deferred rollout plan for v2/v3 kernel mix
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: safely introduce a hybrid kernel execution path that fuses select FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels for decoder-heavy workloads without causing observable latency/quality regressions. This ticket drives the prober harness, signal definitions, and a deferred rollout plan that switches traffic gradually while maintaining easy rollback. Background: previous rollouts of v3-only paths produced intermittent latency spikes for long-context chat prefill in ~0.8% of traces. Rather than blunt switches, the plan here performs live probing with staged weight adjustments and conservative canary thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prober can classify per-request best kernel (v2/v3/hybrid) with <2% false positive on known gold sample set. 2) Canary traffic ramp shows no >5ms p95 increase or >3% throughput drop versus baseline after 1M tokens. 3) Automated rollback triggers operate end-to-end in console (alert -> policy -> rollback). 4) Documentation and runbook updated and verified by oncall.
implementation_steps: Build prober harness that runs lightweight microbenchmarks at request arrival to choose kernel variant
Integrate decision into serving runtime via pluggable kernel adapter interface
Add traffic weighting API to route small percentage to hybrid kernel for canary
Instrument telemetry: per-kernel latencies, tail metrics, token/sec, GPU memory high-water markers
Create canary automation job in console with stepwise weight increases and rollback policies
Run offline A/B sims on representative workload traces (chat, long-prefill, short-response)
Execute internal canary on staging fleet, then small production pilot, then wider rollout
experiment_results: Staging microbench: v3-only wins for small contexts (<128) by 6-9% throughput, but v2 hybrid wins for >2048 by 10% throughput
Replay run (2M tokens): naive v3 rollout caused 7% p95 uplift in chat-prefill traces where batch coalescing occurred
Prober baseline classification accuracy on labeled dataset: 97.4% precision, 95.9% recall
Initial hybrid canary (1% traffic for 24h): no significant error rate increase, p95 delta +1.8ms vs baseline, tokens/sec -1.1%
Memory surface: hybrid path reduced peak workspace by ~12% in long-context runs vs v3-only
blockers: Need small-runtime API change for per-request kernel hints (RFC under review)
GPU scheduler metric visibility gap for prefill-vs-decode separations
Missing automated test for rare interleaved prefill-decode patterns (PR in draft)
